questions.q: GDP measures the total ______ of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year.
questions.e: Gross Domestic Product is the market value of final goods and services produced within the domestic territory in a year.

questions.q: A sustained fall in the general price level of goods and services is called
questions.e: Deflation is a sustained fall in the general price level. Disinflation is only a slowdown in the rate of inflation.

questions.q: NITI Aayog replaced which body in January 2015?
questions.e: NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015 in place of the Planning Commission, which dated from 1950.

questions.q: GST was implemented in India with effect from
questions.e: Goods and Services Tax came into force on 1 July 2017.

questions.q: How many members does the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the RBI have?
questions.e: The MPC has six members: three from the RBI, including the Governor as chairperson, and three nominated by the Central Government.

questions.q: Which of the following is a direct tax?
questions.e: A direct tax is paid by the person on whom it is levied, as with income tax. GST, customs and excise duty are indirect taxes.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India began operations in the year
questions.e: The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934. It was nationalised on 1 January 1949.

questions.q: The back of the ₹500 note of the Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series shows which monument?
questions.e: The ₹500 note carries an image of the Red Fort with the Indian flag. Sanchi Stupa is on ₹200, Rani ki Vav on ₹100 and Konark on ₹10.

questions.q: Fiscal deficit is the excess of total expenditure of the government over its
questions.e: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts), that is, the amount the government must borrow.

questions.q: In India, the money supply measure M3 is commonly known as
questions.e: M3 is broad money, which adds time deposits with banks to M1. M1 is narrow money, and reserve money (M0) is also called high-powered money.

questions.q: The Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61), which stressed rapid industrialisation with priority to heavy industry, was based on the model of
questions.e: The Second Plan followed the Mahalanobis model, favouring capital goods industries. The First Plan used a Harrod–Domar type model.

questions.q: The Imperial Bank of India was renamed the State Bank of India in the year
questions.e: The State Bank of India Act, 1955 converted the Imperial Bank into SBI. The RBI had been formed earlier, in 1935.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Indian currency
I. The ₹1 note is issued by the Reserve Bank of India like all other notes.
II. The ₹1 note is issued by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: The ₹1 note and coins are issued under the authority of the Government of India (Finance Ministry). The RBI issues notes of ₹2 and above.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Planning Commission
I. It was a constitutional body.
II. It was set up in 1950 by an executive resolution of the Government of India.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Planning Commission was neither constitutional nor statutory. It was created by a Cabinet resolution in March 1950.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about GST
I. It is a destination-based tax on consumption.
II. The Centre levies IGST on inter-state supply of goods and services.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: GST is levied where consumption takes place, and IGST is the Centre's levy on inter-state supplies. Both statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)
I. Banks must maintain it only as cash deposited with the RBI.
II. Banks maintain it in liquid assets such as cash, gold and approved securities.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: SLR is held by banks themselves in liquid assets such as cash, gold and government securities. Balances kept with the RBI are the CRR.

questions.q: After the Third Five-Year Plan ended in 1966, planning was suspended and three one-year plans were followed. This period (1966–69) is known as the
questions.e: The failure of the Third Plan, the wars and the drought led to three Annual Plans, called the Plan Holiday. The Fourth Plan began in 1969.

questions.q: A government has total expenditure of ₹500 crore, receipts excluding borrowings of ₹380 crore and interest payments of ₹40 crore. Its primary deficit is
questions.e: Fiscal deficit = 500 − 380 = ₹120 crore. Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments = 120 − 40 = ₹80 crore.

questions.q: If nominal GDP of an economy is ₹600 crore and real GDP is ₹500 crore, the GDP deflator is
questions.e: GDP deflator = (nominal GDP ÷ real GDP) × 100 = (600 ÷ 500) × 100 = 120.

questions.q: Match the Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series notes with the monument shown on the back.
questions.e: ₹10 shows Konark Sun Temple, ₹50 the stone chariot at Hampi, ₹100 Rani ki Vav and ₹200 Sanchi Stupa.
